What can be renamed on its own. ‸ marks the cursor.

=== a plain method
-- script/main --
class Bag { add(): void {} }
export function main(): void { new Bag().ad‸d() }
-- rename --
ok

=== a method that overrides
-- script/main --
class Base { greet(): string { return "a" } }
class Child extends Base { gre‸et(): string { return "b" } }
-- rename --
it overrides Base.greet

=== a method a subclass overrides
-- script/main --
class Base { gre‸et(): string { return "a" } }
class Child extends Base { greet(): string { return "b" } }
-- rename --
Child overrides it

=== a method that implements an interface's
-- script/main --
interface Greeter { greet(): string }
class Hello implements Greeter { gre‸et(): string { return "hi" } }
-- rename --
it implements Greeter.greet

=== a Behaviour method the host calls by name
-- script/main --
import { Greeter } from "test"
export default class Hello implements Greeter {
  greet(name: string): string { return name }
  hel‸lo(): string { return "hi" }
}
-- rename --
it implements Greeter.hello

=== an interface member a class implements
-- script/main --
interface Greeter { gre‸et(): string }
class Hello implements Greeter { greet(): string { return "hi" } }
-- rename --
Hello implements it

=== an interface another extends
-- script/main --
interface Named { na‸me(): string }
interface Person extends Named { age(): number }
-- rename --
Person extends Named
